proposals.ballotLanguage:
Shall Ironwood Area Schools of Gogebic County, Michigan, borrow the sum of not to exceed Twelve Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($12,500,000) and issue its general obligation unlimited tax bonds therefor, in one or more series, for the purpose of:
remodeling, furnishing and refurnishing, and equipping and re-equipping a school building, erecting a school support building; and equipping, developing, and improving athletic fields and facilities, parking areas, driveways, and sites?
The following is for informational purposes only:
The estimated millage that will be levied for the proposed bonds in 2027 is 1.95 mills ($1.95 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a -0- mill net increase over the prior year's levy. The maximum number of years the bonds of any series may be outstanding, exclusive of any refunding, is thirty (30) years. The estimated simple average annual millage anticipated to be required to retire this bond debt is 1.92 mills ($1.92 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation).
The school district does not expect to borrow from the State to pay debt service on the bonds. The total amount of qualified bonds currently outstanding is $670,000. The total amount of qualified loans currently outstanding is $0. The estimated computed millage rate may change based on changes in certain circumstances.
(Pursuant to State law, expenditure of bond proceeds must be audited and the proceeds cannot be used for repair or maintenance costs, teacher, administrator or employee salaries, or other operating expenses.)
proposals.officialTitle: IRONWOOD AREA SCHOOLS OF GOGEBIC COUNTY BOND PROPOSAL
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote authorizes the sale of $12.5 million in bonds, repaid through a property tax levy over the life of the bonds.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote rejects the borrowing — no bonds are issued and no new debt levy is added.
proposals.conservativeView: Bonds commit taxpayers to decades of debt service. Ask whether the project list is needs or wants, whether the district has maintained what it already has, and what the total interest cost will be. "No tax rate increase" often means extending an existing levy for many more years rather than letting it expire.
proposals.progressiveView: Bonds let communities fund major facility needs — safety, infrastructure, aging buildings — spreading the cost over the years the improvements will be used.

'The terms of Office of City Commissioner shall be four years and staggered commencing the first regular meeting following a Commission Election. Transition to staggered terms shall be accomplished by the top three vote getters in the next Election (November 2028) receiving four-year terms (expiring Nov. 2032). The next two…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
SHALL
THE CITY OF IRONWOOD CHARTER PROVIDE FOR STAGGERED FOUR YEAR COMMISSIONER TERMS INSTEAD OF THE CURRENT TWO-YEAR TERMS BY REPLACING THE WORDING OF SECTION 3.5(b) WITH:
'The terms of Office of City Commissioner shall be four years and staggered commencing the first regular meeting following a Commission Election. Transition to staggered terms shall be accomplished by the top three vote getters in the next Election (November 2028) receiving four-year terms (expiring Nov. 2032). The next two vote getters shall receive two-year terms (expiring Nov. 2030). At the November 2030 Election, the top two vote getters will receive four-year terms.'
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote adopts the change described in the ballot language.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote keeps the current rules in place.
proposals.conservativeView: Read the full language carefully. Charter changes are hard to undo; be cautious about proposals that expand government authority, create new boards, or raise spending or borrowing limits.
proposals.progressiveView: Supporters typically argue the change modernizes outdated provisions or improves how local government operates.

proposals.name: Operations Renewal Millage
proposals.description: Shall the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan Constitution on general ad valorem taxes within the Township of Wakefield be increased at 3 mills ($3 per $1,000 of taxable value), subject to any applicable Headlee rollback under Article IX, Section 31 of the Michigan Constitution, and levied for four years 2027, 2028, 2029, and 2030, for general Township operating purposes, thereby raising an estimated $157,459.77 in the first year the millage is levied, this being…
proposals.ballotLanguage: Shall the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan Constitution on general ad valorem taxes within the Township of Wakefield be increased at 3 mills ($3 per $1,000 of taxable value), subject to any applicable Headlee rollback under Article IX, Section 31 of the Michigan Constitution, and levied for four years 2027, 2028, 2029, and 2030, for general Township operating purposes, thereby raising an estimated $157,459.77 in the first year the millage is levied, this being a renewal of the three mills which will expire with the 2026 tax levy.
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote continues the existing levy of 3 mills for 4 years — generally no increase over what you pay now, plus the restored or added amount described.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote lets the current millage expire; the service it funds would need cuts or other revenue.
proposals.conservativeView: Renewals are the least disruptive way to keep a service funded, but every renewal is a chance to ask whether the service is delivering value. Watch for "renewal" proposals that quietly restore Headlee rollbacks — that is a tax increase.
proposals.progressiveView: Keeps an existing, voter-approved service funded at the same rate with no new tax.
